## Historical audit: S0221

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_1/results/r2/fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_80372956/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines and supplied character ranges.

| Aspect | Evidence and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Goal | The instruction was to reconstruct an indoor photograph as separate 3D meshes, matching geometry, materials, camera and framing; the reference image itself is not visible in the supplied audit text. The student’s scene name and code indicate an interpretation of a timber ceiling and starburst chandelier, not independently verified image content (line 1, [0,5604); line 3, [0,7062)). |
| Actual construction | The student produced one program defining separate ceiling and chandelier assets, with many boards, rafters, ties, joints, rods and globes. It specified a suspension and arms positioned around a central globe; actual connectivity and occlusion were not geometrically checked. The chandelier was modeled in a hanging, radially arranged pose; its match to the reference is unknown (line 3, [0,7062)). |
| Materials and view | The program used colored surfaces, assigned metallic and roughness values conditionally, and added geometric highlights; no image textures were specified. It set an upward camera, three area lights and Cycles rendering. Whether materials, camera, lighting or rendering match the photograph—or have visual defects—is unknown without an image (line 3, [0,7062)). |
| Execution and validation | The runner launched Blender for step 1, but reported `ok: false`, a timeout after approximately 516.7 seconds, empty stdout/stderr and `image: null` (lines 4–5, [0,7692), [0,1063)). No successful build, render inspection, revision or final `DONE` is visible. This is a **technical interruption**, not evidence of geometric algorithm failure or an empty patch; reconstruction quality and formal success remain unknown. |
| Teacher and exploration | No teacher message, detection, diagnosis, proposed update or student adoption appears in this trace. The student independently generated the program in one observable CLI turn with zero tool calls; the record shows one execution and no subsequent exploratory iteration (line 2, [0,2840); lines 3–5). |

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, a generated scene program and a launched render are not visual validation; timeout should be distinguished from a proven modeling error. Task-specific choices include the two-tier chandelier, timber roof, upward viewpoint and metallic finish. A plausible but unverified hypothesis is that scene complexity or render settings contributed to the timeout: the empty logs do not establish its cause. Neither the reference nor a rendered result is available here to assess object count, appearance, part connections, pose or framing accuracy.
